intro: These articles are for shops that make their own listing photos and short ads. They cover a usable source photo, a creator-style ad, a pre-publish check, a launch reveal, and a person wearing the item without a shoot.
Read the piece that matches the job, then make the file in the tool it names. You download it and post it yourself.

faq.q: Where do I start if I am new to this?
faq.a: If you only have a phone photo, start with the photography article. If you already have a clear product photo and need a clip, start with the ad article.

faq.q: Should I read the article or open the tool?
faq.a: Read the article for the job, then open the tool it names. The article explains the job. The tool is where the file is made.

faq.q: What should I check before I publish?
faq.a: Use the checklist article. Confirm the product matches what you ship, watch a clip more than once, and add prices only after download.

faq.q: Which piece is about a launch?
faq.a: The unboxing article plans three clips around launch day, from one product photo. You add the offer after download.

faq.q: Can I show the item on a person without a shoot?
faq.a: Yes. One article shows how to start from a clear garment photo and describe the person and the setting. Check the fit before you post.

faq.q: How much does a photo or a clip cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the cost before you start, and a failed job returns its credits.

faq.q: Are the people in the clips real customers?
faq.a: No. The person is generated. Do not give them a name or a line that says they bought the product.

faq.q: Which size should I use for TikTok or a product grid?
faq.a: Product photos come out square. Video frames are 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4. The ad-size guide and the platform pages say which frame a placement uses.
